references.text: Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and gave them the status of his own sons, which resulted in Joseph's descendants becoming two tribes instead of one.
Joseph's sons according to their clans were Manasseh and Ephraim, confirming that Joseph's descendants formed two tribes.
The Levites were to receive cities to live in from the inheritance of the other tribes, with pastureland around the cities for their livestock and property.
The heads of the Levite families came to Joshua and were assigned cities from the inheritance of the other tribes, as the Lord had commanded.
The Levites were not to have any share of the land as an inheritance, but were to receive tithes from Israel as their inheritance.
The tribe of Levi received no inheritance with their brothers, because the Lord is their inheritance.
Joseph had two sons in Egypt: Manasseh and Ephraim, who became the ancestors of the two tribes that bore their names.
Only the tribe of Levi received no inheritance, because the Lord's fire offering is their inheritance.
